skill.name: personwise-content-repurposing
skill.description: Repurpose recordings, transcripts, and long-form materials into grounded interactive PersonWise courses with reviewed outlines, scripts, visuals, and access controls.
skill.summary: Turn existing source material into an askable digital-human course.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fixed validation commands, conventional installer paths, and signed descriptor data. The skill still installs unauditable remote executables and uploads selected source documents to PersonWise, creating supply-chain and confidentiality risks.

remediation.issue: The bundled bootstraps install downloaded executables that are not available for marketplace review, while native signature enforcement is disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Publish reproducible source and build provenance, then enforce detached release signatures or native platform signatures before installing every downloaded executable.

remediation.issue: Selected documents are uploaded to a third-party PersonWise service and may contain confidential material.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination and selected files before upload, obtain explicit upload consent, and document retention, access, deletion, and data-processing terms.

finding_verdicts.reason: The PowerShell installer downloads a platform executable from a fixed PersonWise HTTPS host. Size and hash pinning reduce tampering, but remote executable installation remains a supply-chain risk.
The substitution only reads the operating system and architecture with fixed uname arguments for platform selection. It does not evaluate user-controlled command text.
The substitution uses fixed uname arguments to gate a signature check. No untrusted value becomes a command or option.
The substitution uses fixed uname arguments to choose the conventional user installation directory. It has no command-injection path.
The fixed printf and tr pipeline removes control characters from a quoted directory value. This is validation, not dynamic command execution.
The fixed ls command records the validated installation directory inode for a later race check. The path is quoted and is not executable input.
The substitution hashes a quoted existing executable through a fixed helper. It validates an approved upgrade target and does not execute the target.
The fixed mktemp command creates a private working directory under the validated target directory. Its template is controlled by the installer.
The fixed wc and tr pipeline measures the downloaded archive before extraction. The quoted file path cannot alter the command.
The substitution computes a SHA-256 digest for the quoted archive and compares it with a pinned value. It is an integrity check.
The fixed tar listing reads an archive only after size and SHA-256 verification. The archive path is quoted and the exact entries are checked.
The substitution hashes the extracted executable and compares it with a pinned digest. It does not execute the downloaded candidate.
The fixed uname result and static signature status only decide whether platform signature checks run. No dynamic command text is evaluated.
The fixed codesign pipeline reads the signing identity of the quoted candidate. It is used only when native verification is enabled.
The fixed ls command verifies that the installation directory inode did not change. This is a local race-condition defense.
The fixed hash helper verifies that the existing target did not change before replacement. The quoted path is not interpreted as a command.
The shell installer downloads a platform executable from a fixed PersonWise HTTPS host. Size and hash pinning reduce tampering, but remote executable installation remains a supply-chain risk.
HOME/.local/bin is the conventional per-user executable directory. The installer validates that the directory is absolute and not a symbolic link.
HOME/.local/bin is a conventional per-user installation directory, not covert storage. The path is validated before use.
The hidden name is a temporary installer workspace created with mktemp and removed by a trap. It does not provide persistence or conceal durable data.
The /dev/null redirection suppresses output while checking for an available SHA-256 utility. It neither reads sensitive device data nor writes persistent data.
The /dev/null redirection suppresses output while checking for an available SHA-256 utility. It neither reads sensitive device data nor writes persistent data.
mktemp creates a unique installer workspace in the validated user bin directory. A trap removes it on exit, and paths remain quoted.
The hard link atomically installs a verified candidate only when the target is absent. Failure on an occupied target prevents overwrite and limits race exposure.
ls -id reads only the chosen installation directory inode to detect replacement during installation. It does not survey the wider system.
ls -id reads only the chosen installation directory inode to detect replacement during installation. It does not survey the wider system.
spctl assesses the local candidate executable with macOS Gatekeeper. It is a signature policy check, not network discovery.

content.user_title: Turn Existing Content into an Interactive Course
content.value_statement: Recordings and transcripts are difficult to reuse as structured learning. This skill converts supplied material into a grounded, interactive PersonWise course.
actual_capabilities: Transforms supplied recordings, transcripts, talks, and documents into a structured teaching arc.
Creates PersonWise course blueprints with learner, outcome, page count, visuals, presenter, and access settings.
Uploads user-selected source documents and monitors their processing status.
Reviews outlines, scripts, slide text, images, and factual support at workflow checkpoints.
Publishes private or link-access courses when the user requests that access mode.
Resumes, repairs, refines, and queries existing PersonWise course runs.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser OAuth, a PersonWise account, and available course credits.
Uses an external PersonWise service and may upload selected source documents.
Cannot verify claims that the supplied source material does not support.
Image review requires a vision-capable agent; otherwise visual inspection is recorded as not performed.

use_cases.title: Repurpose a Webinar
use_cases.description: Convert a recorded webinar and transcript into an interactive course with source-grounded questions and answers.

use_cases.title: Reuse Expert Talks
use_cases.description: Turn internal expert presentations into structured learning with reviewed scripts, visuals, and assessments.

use_cases.title: Create Customer Education
use_cases.description: Transform long-form product material into an askable course with controlled access and a shareable delivery link.

prompt_templates.title: Repurpose One Transcript
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this transcript into a grounded interactive course. Keep only supported claims and default access to private.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one clean transcript and wants a simple course.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Webinar
prompt_templates.prompt: Repurpose my webinar recording, transcript, and slides into a course. Preserve the core framework and flag dated claims for review.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants to reuse a webinar with several source files.

prompt_templates.title: Build for a Defined Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an eight-page course for new customers from these materials. Include a self-check, use our branding, and request link access.
prompt_templates.scenario: A content owner has a target audience, page count, and delivery goal.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Publish a Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume this PersonWise course. Verify source status, review each checkpoint, correct unsupported content, inspect available visuals, and publish only after playability is confirmed.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs controlled recovery, review, and publication.

output_examples.input: Repurpose a product webinar transcript into a private course for new customers.
output_examples.output: A private interactive course with a focused thesis, product framework, supported examples, audience questions, self-check, and verified viewing link.

output_examples.input: Turn a recorded leadership talk and its slides into an eight-page course.
output: An eight-page teaching arc based on the speaker's strongest supported ideas.
Reviewed slide text and narration aligned with the supplied talk and visuals.
A concise report with source status, review results, course state, and access details.

best_practices: Provide complete source files and identify the intended learners, outcome, language, page count, and access mode.
Confirm time-sensitive claims and remove unsupported statements before publication.
Review every outline, script, and visual checkpoint before advancing the course.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent current facts, product features, screenshots, or audience data.
Do not upload files that the user did not select without explicit approval.
Do not create replacement runs to bypass source failures, conflicts, limits, or review checkpoints.

faq.question: What source material can I use?
faq.answer: You can provide recordings, transcripts, talks, documents, slides, and selected reference images.

faq.question: Does the skill create facts that are missing?
faq.answer: No. It removes unsupported claims and flags dated or time-sensitive information for confirmation.

faq.question: Does it require a PersonWise account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need browser OAuth, a compatible PersonWise CLI, and sufficient course credits.

faq.question: Are my files uploaded?
faq.answer: Selected documents may be uploaded to PersonWise for processing. Review confidential material and service terms before use.

faq.question: Can the course be public?
faq.answer: The default is private. The skill can enable link access or submit to Topics when you request that target.

faq.question: Can it update an existing course?
faq.answer: Yes. It can resume, repair, refine, publish, change access, or query a course using current workflow permissions.
